name: Anomalous Origin of Coronary Artery from the Pulmonary Artery

criteria.description: Identification of coronary artery originating anomalously from the pulmonary artery on imaging
Evidence of myocardial ischemia or infarction on clinical or imaging evaluation
Presence of collateral coronary circulation from the normally originating coronary artery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anomalous coronary artery origin from the pulmonary artery plus evidence of myocardial ischemia or infarction
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily confirmed by echocardiography, cardiac MRI, or coronary angiography.

pathognomonic.notes: Often presents as irritability or feeding difficulties due to ischemic pain
searchTerms: reduced blood flow to infant heart

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mitral valve regurgitation secondary to papillary muscle ischemia
pathognomonic.notes: Commonly associated with left ventricular dysfunction
searchTerms: leaky mitral valve from heart muscle damage
mitral valve leakage due to ischemia

common.notes: Includes tachypnea, poor feeding, and failure to thrive
More evident in older children or adults with undiagnosed condition
May be reported in older children

occasional.notes: Includes ventricular tachycardia and premature ventricular contractions
Due to transient ischemia or arrhythmia

rare.notes: May develop secondary to increased pulmonary blood flow

searchTerms: bulging area in left heart chamber

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits secondary to embolic events

laboratory: Elevated cardiac biomarkers (troponin, CK-MB) during ischemic episodes
Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing anomalous coronary artery origin and left ventricular dysfunction
Coronary angiography confirming anomalous origin and collateral circulation
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial ischemia and fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; sporadic congenital anomaly
other: Electrocardiogram showing signs of ischemia or infarction

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atherosclerotic plaques on imaging
Systolic compression of coronary artery segment

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe myocardial ischemia in infancy
Progressive left ventricular dysfunction despite medical therapy
Sudden cardiac arrest or unexplained syncope in young patient
references: Wesselhoeft H, Fawcett JS, Johnson AL. Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary trunk. Its clinical spectrum, pathology, and pathophysiology, based on a review of 140 cases with seven further cases. Circulation. 1968;38(2):403-425.

Moodie DS, Fyfe D, Gill CC, Cook SA, Vohra HA, Ross DN. Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery (Bland-White-Garland syndrome) in adult patients: long-term follow-up after surgery. Am Heart J. 1983;106(2):381-388.
Ginde S, et al. Anomalous origin of the left coronary artery from the pulmonary artery: diagnosis and surgical management. J Card Surg. 2019;34(6):391-398.
